clue.text: Advantageous to be young with a lisp  …

indicators.note: a lisp turns every s into a th, so the word is judged by how a lisper would pronounce it

blocks.note: young means youthful, and a lisper saying the needed word lands on exactly that sound

explanation.surface: A child with a lisp is said to have some hidden advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: Say USEFUL with a lisp and the s becomes th: 'youthful'. The clue's 'a lisp' is reused by 5 across, hence the trailing dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Something advantageous serves a purpose and helps you, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Spoke, being agile

indicators.note: the setter treats this as saying one word is being another, so part of the first is swapped for a synonym

blocks.note: the whole word, read as an S followed by a separate four-letter word
the tail of the word; to poke about is to pry, so a synonym takes its place while the S stays

explanation.walkthrough: A loose clue: read 'Spoke' as S + POKE, and replace POKE with its synonym PRY (both mean to nose into things). The surface suggests a wheel's spoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone, usually older, who is nimble and lively on their feet.

clue.text: The man's in France getting a dealership

indicators.note: one thing sitting inside another means its letters go within the other's

blocks.note: the country, taken as written
belonging to the man is 'his'

explanation.surface: A man in France lands himself a car dealership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In France' reads as a location but tells you to put the letters inside FRANCE, between the C and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A franchise is a licence to sell a company's goods, so a dealership is a typical example.

clue.text: Stan's bay

definitions.note: possessive: Stan's surname, i.e. the surname of Stan of Laurel and Hardy

blocks.note: first meaning: the surname of the comic actor Stan of the double act with Oliver Hardy
second meaning: the bay tree, whose leaves flavour cooking

explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a stretch of coast owned by someone called Stan. Stan Laurel was the thin half of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay tree is the sweet laurel, and Stan Laurel carried the same word as his surname.

clue.text: …  leaving spiritualism to go off for some pudding

indicators.note: something leaving a place departs from it, so those letters are taken away
food that goes off turns bad, and the remaining letters likewise spoil into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; the letters L, I, S, P are then removed, carried over from the previous clue

explanation.surface: Someone abandons spiritualism and goes off to eat dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 1 across: its 'lisp' is what leaves SPIRITUALISM, and the remaining eight letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert of coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone, an example of a pudding.

clue.text: Always evens out after a couple of dozen

indicators.note: things put out of place are disordered, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: two dozen is twenty-four
taken as written

explanation.surface: Like a gambler, someone always backs evens once they've bet a couple of dozen times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evens out' sounds like balancing things up; here 'out' is the signal to rearrange the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-four seven means all hours of every day of the week, so it is an idiom for constantly.

clue.text: Put limits on dress, strip clothing off before court

indicators.note: clothing is the outer layer, so stripping it off removes each word's outside letters

blocks.note: the word without its first and last letters
the word without its first and last letters
CT is the standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A dress code is imposed: no undressing in front of the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' looks like the instruction, but it is fodder; both 'dress' and 'strip' lose their outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict something is to confine it within bounds, a direct synonym for limiting it.

clue.text: New Zealander chairman oddly missing train

indicators.note: with the odd-numbered letters gone, only the even-placed ones remain

blocks.note: Chairman Mao Zedong, leader of Communist China
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A New Zealander's train is missing its chairman, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chairman oddly' seems to belong together, but the oddness applies to 'train'; the chairman is Mao.
explanation.definitionFit: The Māori are the indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand, so one of them is a New Zealander.

clue.text: Fresh plot twist involving a thief

indicators.note: a twist turns things round, so these letters are wrung into a new order
to involve is to wrap something up inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a means one, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A new plot twist in a crime story brings in a thief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh plot twist' reads as storytelling; it is anagram fodder and signal, with 'a' as I (one) inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoplifter steals goods from a store, so is one particular kind of thief.

clue.text: Being true to form after running race

indicators.note: running freely, letters are loosened from their order
forming something means shaping it anew, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An athlete stays true to form after running a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'True to form' looks like a set phrase, but 'to form' rearranges TRUE; 'running' rearranges RACE, which comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A being is any living thing, and creature is a common synonym for such a living thing.

clue.text: Boy consuming cannabis precisely

indicators.note: consuming something takes it inside, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: a boy can be a son
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A lad smoking cannabis, described with precision.
explanation.walkthrough: Pot is common slang for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is an informal British idiom for exactly right or accurate.

clue.text: Sofa in box with lid free to be moved

indicators.note: letters that are moved are shifted about into a new arrangement

blocks.note: a chest is a large box
taken as written

explanation.surface: Delivery men find a sofa packed in a box whose lid comes off for moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' joins the definition to the wordplay, and 'with' simply adds the second piece after the box.
explanation.definitionFit: A chesterfield is a deep-buttoned leather sofa with arms and back of equal height.

clue.text: With one movement, fluent about movie's completion

indicators.note: a single letter shifting its place counts as rearranging the word
to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: taken as written
a movie is a film

explanation.surface: A smooth single movement brings a film to its finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With one movement' is a gentle signal: only the U shifts, jumping ahead of the L. The 's in 'movie's' stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulfilment is the carrying out or achieving of something, so it matches finishing a task.

clue.text: Apple mountain

blocks.note: first meaning: a sweet, crisp variety of eating apple
second meaning: Japan's highest peak, a volcano

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like one description, perhaps a heap of fruit; they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fuji apple variety was bred in Japan and named after its famous volcanic peak.

clue.text: Confront boost in cosmetic surgery

blocks.note: to face something is to confront it
a lift is a boost

explanation.surface: A patient confronts a boost in cosmetic surgery bookings.
explanation.walkthrough: Two plain synonyms placed side by side, with 'in' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A facelift is an operation to tighten skin and remove wrinkles, one example of plastic surgery.

clue.text: Secures part of Batman's outfit for picture

blocks.note: to land a deal or prize is to secure it
Batman wears a cape

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a piece of the Batman costume for a photo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' looks like it asks for some letters of a word, but it simply points to a garment Batman wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a painting or photograph of countryside scenery, so a type of picture.

clue.text: They rise in surprise as Matilda reads aloud!

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the phrase is judged by its sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: Matilda is the setter, so she is I; to read casually is to browse

explanation.surface: Eyebrows go up when the setter Matilda reads aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name or pseudonym to mean I or ME; here Matilda is the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: People raise their brows when astonished, so they are the facial features that go up when surprised.

clue.text: 'Age before beauty', says V?

indicators.note: what someone says is heard, so the sound matters rather than spelling

blocks.note: in the alphabet V comes straight after U, so V could describe itself that way

explanation.surface: The letter V politely lets someone go first, citing the old courtesy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Age before beauty' is a jokey phrase used when holding a door for someone; the letter V follows U in the alphabet, and U is said like 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are polite formulas for letting another person pass through ahead of you.

clue.text: Born and died in poverty

blocks.note: née, used before a woman's maiden name, means born
D is the standard abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A life story: born and died penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Born' tempts you to use N, but it is NEE; 'and' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Need as a noun means lack of money or necessities, the state of being poor.

clue.text: Kind of language used by the bloke with tea?

blocks.note: a bloke is a man, referred to as he
a brew is British slang for a cup of tea

explanation.surface: A man over a cuppa uses a particular kind of language.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'a brew' is everyday slang for a pot or cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebrew is the Semitic tongue of Israel and of Jewish scripture, one example of a language.

clue.text: Hits sources of obstruction clutching bosom

indicators.note: clutching means holding tight, so one piece grips another inside it

blocks.note: things that block are blockers
the bust is the chest or bosom

explanation.surface: Something strikes the cause of a blockage while hugging it to the chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hits' looks like a verb about striking, but it is the definition as a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Blockbusters are hugely successful films or books, so they are commercial hits.

clue.text: Links from China with a promotion

indicators.note: a promotion moves something up, so one letter climbs higher in the down entry

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A firm with links in China gets a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter A of CHINA is 'promoted', moving up two places in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain is a series of connected links, so links collectively make one.

clue.text: Business policy

blocks.note: first meaning: a trade or occupation
second meaning: an official position or stance, such as a party's agreed position

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like a phrase about company rules; they are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Your line can be your occupation, and a party line is its agreed stance on issues.

clue.text: See about fixing gate smoothly, leaving no gaps

indicators.note: fixing something puts it back in order, so the letters are rearranged
to be about something is to go around it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: lo is an old word for look or see
taken as written

explanation.surface: A handyman arranges to mend a gate so it closes smoothly without gaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoothly, leaving no gaps' sounds like the repair; it is the musical definition. LO, as in 'lo and behold', means see.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is a musical direction to play notes smoothly joined, with no breaks between them.

clue.text: Word for word, very bad time, endlessly

indicators.note: without an end, each word loses its final letter

blocks.note: the word without its last letter
the word without its last letter
the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: Quoting someone exactly about a very bad time that seemed to go on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' sounds like the bad time dragging on, but it trims the last letter from each of the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbatim means in exactly the same words as originally used, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Substitutes put up with evil

definitions.note: a verb here: takes someone's place

blocks.note: to stand something is to put up with it
sin is wickedness

explanation.surface: Replacement players tolerate wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' reads as one phrase meaning tolerate; the setter splits it, using 'put up' for STAND and 'with' as the join.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand in is to act as a replacement, the same as the verb substitutes.

clue.text: Worked in the garden seeing small early signs of Dutch elm disease

indicators.note: the earliest sign of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: wee is Scottish and informal British for small
initial letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A gardener tidies the beds after spotting the first hints of Dutch elm disease.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch elm disease is a fungal infection that killed most British elms; here it only supplies three initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeding is pulling unwanted plants out of beds, a typical gardening task, so it means did garden work.
